title: Noah Calls His People Day and Night

paragraphs.text: The surah ends with a final instruction. The Prophet is told to leave the disbelievers to their empty talk and their games, and to let them enjoy themselves for a while, until they finally meet the Day they have been promised. On that Day they will come out of their graves quickly, rushing forward as if they were racing toward an idol set up for them. Their eyes will be lowered in shame, and humiliation will cover them. That is the very Day they were warned about again and again.

A new surah tells the story of Noah. Allah sent him to his people with the instruction to warn them before a painful punishment reached them. Noah obeyed. He stood before his people and told them plainly that he had come to them as a clear warner, hiding nothing of the message. He called them to worship Allah, to fear Him and to obey him as their messenger. If they did so, Allah would forgive their sins and allow them to live until a time already fixed. But he also reminded them that when the time set by Allah arrives, it can never be delayed, if only they understood.

Later Noah turned to his Lord in prayer and described his long struggle with his people. He said that he had called his people night and day, but his call only made them run further away. Every time he invited them so that Allah might forgive them, they pushed their fingers into their ears, wrapped themselves in their clothes, refused stubbornly and showed great arrogance. He tried every method. He called them openly in public, he made announcements, and he also spoke to them privately in secret. He told them to ask forgiveness from their Lord, because He is always ready to forgive. In return, Allah would send them plentiful rain from the sky, increase their wealth and children, and give them gardens and rivers. Noah then asked them why they did not show Allah the respect and greatness He deserves, when He had created them in stages, one after another.
